Mighty Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat Drags Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 and It Was a Comedy of Errors
18 photos
Photo: Wheels / YouTube
The videographer behind the ' Wheels ' channel on YouTube recently took a detour around BMP – aka Bradenton Motorsports Park in Florida for some cool excerpts from the FL2K competition, but now they're back at The Strip at Las Vegas Motor Speedway.
So, after the intermezzo at BMP, it’s time to head back to The Strip at Las Vegas Motor Speedway as the videographer caught a couple of traditional fighters that were ready to bring honor to their brands – or so we thought, at least initially.
First, let’s meet the protagonists. In the left lane resides a defunct Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat , which has a 6.2-liter supercharged Hemi V8 with various levels of power, depending on the exact model year and versions. This particular unit comes dark and menacing, but it also has contrasting elements: the silver wrap on the hood, roof, and trunk combined with dual black stripes, as well as the gold rear alloy wheels.
Meanwhile, its opponent, the S550 Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 , is dressed in satin black and also has its own contrasting elements: orange trim on the brake calipers, badges, or the rear wing, among other places. Both looked menacingly sporty and ready to make their fans proud, of course. But looks can be deceiving when the drivers don’t really know exactly what they are doing.
And this is a good example of a comedy of errors: they lined up properly, but only the Shelby took off at the green light while the Dodge was still dozing off for one reason or the other. No worries, as the GT500 almost came to a complete stop a few feet in front of the Dodge, then accelerated again after seeing the Mopar take the point.
We thought it was over for the Blue Oval, but no, the comedy was still going on: the Shelby accelerated heavily and managed to recover the lost distance and beat the Hellcat to the finish line, as the latter looked like it was out for a cruise, not at a quarter-mile dragstrip competition. In the end, though, none of them impressed us following this major debacle: 13.37s at 121 mph versus 13.65s at just 99 mph.
These figures aren’t worthy of the Hellcat and Shelby GT500 names, for sure, right? Anyway, over on the streets, the Blue Oval representative is doing much better these days than Dodge’s. That’s because the Challenger is retired, and the eighth generation Charger can’t make up for the lost ground compared to the S650 Ford Mustang.
As such, during the third quarter of the year, the S650 absolutely crushed its Charger competition as far as the ICE models are concerned. Ford sold almost 10k Mustang units, while Dodge only reached 3,446 sales in the quarter with the Hurricane-equipped Charger.
